subject: GCP private offer: proposed commit rephasing and sell-through plan
messages:
From: Sara Yates <sara@orion-analytics.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com, procurement@orion-analytics.com
Cc: linus.evans@gcp-partner.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer drawdown - request to rephase commit

Diego,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're aligned on the technical fit, but procurement asked me to reach out with a pragmatic ask: our CFO wants to rephase the original commit so that 60% of the committed credits are available in Q4 and the remainder in Q1 instead of a straight evenly-spread draw. That helps our quarterly forecasting and gets legal comfortable with the amortization.

Can Redwood confirm whether that rephasing is acceptable on the private offer, and if possible provide an updated drawdown schedule and invoice cadence? We have an active co-sell engagement with GCP and Linus is on the thread for marketplace invoicing implications.

Attached: Orion_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, redlines)
Attachment stub: commit_schedule_v2.xlsx

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like something to sign by the end of next week.

— Sara
Procurement, Orion Analytics

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Yates <sara@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com, ben.carter@redwood.inference.com, linus.evans@gcp-partner.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer drawdown - request to rephase commit

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. We can support a rephasing but need to align a couple of operational details so invoices and marketplace redemption behave as you expect. High level:

- We can split the committed credits 60% / 40% across the dates you proposed.
- Need to confirm whether Orion wants an upfront invoice for the Q4 tranche or prefers invoicing delivered consumption monthly against the reserved credit.
- Co-sell: when credits are pulled via the marketplace, GCP invoicing rules may require specific SKU mapping — Marissa, can you confirm the best path here?
- Legal: our standard private-offer amendment covers rephasing; would like to avoid changing termination clauses.

Next steps I propose: Diego to send a redline-friendly amendment, Marissa to confirm marketplace invoice mapping, Ben to confirm billing and revenue recognition impact, Tessa to coordinate DocuSign timeline. If all agree, Sara signs and we submit the revised private offer to GCP for acceptance.

I attached a draft amendment with the proposed dates and a one-page summary for procurement to share with finance.

— Diego
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: RDW_PrivateOffer_Amendment_draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com, Sara Yates <sara@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com, ben.carter@redwood.inference.com, linus.evans@gcp-partner.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer drawdown - request to rephase commit

Diego / Sara — quick notes from the marketplace side:

- We can map the committed credits to the "redwood-private-credits" SKU and request a staged redemption schedule during private offer activation. That will create predictable redemption accounting on GCP.
- Invoice mechanics: if Orion prefers, we can set an upfront prepay invoice for the 60% tranche (due on effective date) and then monthly consumption statements against the remaining 40% until it's consumed. If Orion wants the entire commit recognized as deferred revenue on their side, they'll need an invoice for the full amount upfront — confirm which treatment procurement/fins prefer.
- Co-sell credits: Linus — to ensure GCP co-sell linkage, we need the marketplace offering ID in the amendment; I've flagged that for our legal to include.

I'll add a short table to the amendment showing exact dates and invoice triggers once Diego posts the final numbers.

— Marissa
Director, Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, Sara Yates <sara@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com, linus.evans@gcp-partner.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer drawdown - request to rephase commit

Sara — quick clarification on billing that will help procurement:

Option A (preferred for predictability): Redwood issues a single invoice for 60% (Q4 tranche) on the effective date; GCP then enables redemption against that tranche. Remaining 40% is invoiced as either a single invoice at the start of Q1 or invoiced monthly as consumption draws it down. This approach minimizes month-to-month invoice reconciliation for Orion.

Option B (preferred for cash management): Invoice consumption monthly against the committed cap; Orion pays as consumption happens but redemption guarantees the reserved capacity. This is operationally lighter for Redwood but increases Orion's monthly cash flow variability.

If Orion wants to sign by next Friday, we'll need confirmation on Option A vs B by Thursday EOD to get legal and finance to finalize the amendment and the DocuSign packet.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Yates <sara@orion-analytics.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com, ben.carter@redwood.inference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com, linus.evans@gcp-partner.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer drawdown - request to rephase commit

Diego / Team — thanks, this is exactly what procurement needed. We prefer Option A (60% upfront invoice, 40% invoiced at Q1 start). Procurement confirms they can sign by Friday if the amendment includes the staged invoice schedule and language that the co-sell linkage will be preserved.

Please send the updated amendment and DocuSign link; I'll route it through our CFO for signature.

Thanks everyone — Sara
Procurement, Orion Analytics
